event_toll.why: 球球畫成冷灰色、深灰條紋、白臉（應是參考圖的淡奶油色、灰褐條紋）；沒有「轉角」，山賊喊得大聲但腿沒在抖（文字：兩條腿卻抖個不停）。山賊長相維持原本這隻。
event_toll.scene: SETTING: a small patch of grey flagstone floor with a few tufts of green grass, and on the RIGHT the corner of a ruined wall of stacked mossy grey stone blocks - the same flagstones and stone blocks as in reference image 2. The orange tabby BANDIT (EXACTLY the bandit of reference image 2: orange tabby with darker orange stripes, a black headband tied with two long black tails, a torn sleeveless brown vest with ragged edges, a black sash belt) has just stepped out from that wall corner and blocks the way. He grips a long thin plain wooden staff upright with BOTH paws, its bottom end resting on the floor; the staff is much longer than he is - its top end rises far above his ears. His mouth is wide open, shouting loudly, eyebrows angry - but his two legs are trembling with fear: knees bent inward and knocking together, short curved shake lines on both sides of his legs, a big sweat drop on his forehead. On the LEFT, a few steps away, Qiuqiu stands facing him, calm and unimpressed: both eyes half-lidded (the same), a small flat mouth. His left paw rests on a small brown drawstring pouch of dried fish tied at his black sash; his right paw hangs relaxed at his side. QIUQIU'S COLOURS: his fur is the warm pale pinkish-cream of reference image 1 with grey-brown stripes - NOT cool grey, NOT dark grey stripes; his face is the same pale cream as his head, with only the small white muzzle of reference image 1.

event_toll_r0.why: 球球冷灰色；照結果文字重對：山賊把小魚乾數了三遍才讓路，球球不耐煩地等（舊圖球球豎單指指著山賊）。山賊長相維持原本這隻。
event_toll_r0.scene: SETTING: the same grey flagstone floor patch and the same corner of ruined mossy stone-block wall as in reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event). The same orange tabby BANDIT as in reference image 3 (orange tabby, black headband with two long black tails, torn sleeveless brown vest, black sash belt) squats on the floor in front of the wall corner, busily counting the dried fish Qiuqiu has just paid: many small dried fish lie in neat rows on the flagstones in front of him, and he taps one of them with his paw, concentrating hard - eyes fixed on the fish, lips pressed together, a sweat drop. His long thin wooden staff lies flat on the floor behind him. On the LEFT, Qiuqiu stands waiting impatiently: both paws on his hips, eyes narrowed (both the same), an annoyed small frown, his right foot tapping (two short tap lines beside the foot). His small brown drawstring fish pouch hangs at his black sash, now flat and nearly empty. QIUQIU'S COLOURS: his fur is the warm pale pinkish-cream of reference image 1 with grey-brown stripes - NOT cool grey; his face is the same pale cream as his head, with only the small white muzzle of reference image 1.
refs: the main picture of this same event: copy its flagstone floor, the corner of the mossy stone-block wall and the orange bandit's look (and his long thin staff) exactly. Take only the setting and the bandit's look, not the poses.

event_blocked_r0.why: 球球冷灰色；卷軸攤開、畫面那面朝觀眾，也沒畫出結果文字的「腳下一滑滾到垃圾山另一邊、坐起來揉肩膀、卷軸好好抱在懷裡」。
event_blocked_r0.scene: SETTING: the SAME big junk pile as in reference image 2 (the main picture of this same event): broken brown wooden planks, wooden crates, a wooden barrel and grey rocks heaped up against grey stone steps, a blank wooden sign board stuck in its top (no writing on it), two lit wall torches. This picture shows the moment after Qiuqiu grabbed the scroll, slipped and tumbled all the way down to the OTHER side of the pile: the junk pile fills the left and middle of the picture; at its right foot, on a small patch of stone floor, Qiuqiu has just SAT UP on the floor, his legs sprawled out in front of him. His RIGHT paw rubs his LEFT shoulder, both eyes squeezed shut the same way in pain, mouth in a wincing grimace, a small tear at one eye corner. His LEFT arm hugs a ROLLED-UP, closed paper scroll tied with a red string tightly against his chest - the scroll is safe in his arm and NOT opened. Two loose planks and a few pebbles have slid down the slope right beside him, and a small puff of dust hangs next to him. QIUQIU'S COLOURS: his fur is the warm pale pinkish-cream of reference image 1 with grey-brown stripes - NOT cool grey; his face is the same pale cream as his head, with only the small white muzzle of reference image 1.

event_rat_stall.why: 球球冷灰色、白臉；老鼠沒有「叫賣時悄悄把咬過的一面轉向背後」的動作，照主文重對。老鼠與攤車長相沿用舊圖。
event_rat_stall.scene: SETTING on a small patch of stone floor: the small wooden two-wheeled pushcart stall of reference image 3 (wooden cart bed with a torn dark-blue cloth hanging on its front, two wooden wheels, a pair of wooden push handles on its left end). Six white rice balls (onigiri) with black seaweed strips sit on the cart; several of them have a clear BITE taken out of them - a bitten-off notch with little tooth marks. The scruffy grey RAT stall-keeper of reference image 3 (grey fur, big pink ears, pink nose, long pink tail, a brown headband, a torn brown patched vest) stands behind the cart at its push handles, holding one handle with his left paw. He is hawking loudly: mouth open in a big salesman grin, while his eyes slide sideways slyly. At the same time his RIGHT paw sneakily turns one bitten rice ball around on the cart, so that its bitten side faces away from Qiuqiu, toward the rat himself. On the RIGHT, Qiuqiu stands facing the cart, leaning forward a little, both eyes narrowed with suspicion at the rice balls, his right paw curled closed under his chin (no finger raised). QIUQIU'S COLOURS: his fur is the warm pale pinkish-cream of reference image 1 with grey-brown stripes - NOT cool grey; his face is the same pale cream as his head, with only the small white muzzle of reference image 1.
refs: the OLD version of this same picture: copy the grey RAT stall-keeper's look and his wooden pushcart with the rice balls exactly. Take ONLY the rat and the cart. The cat in it is drawn with WRONG cool-grey colours and a white face - do not copy that cat at all; Qiuqiu's look comes only from reference image 1.

event_lost_kitten.why: 球球冷灰色、白臉；照主文重對：小黑貓坐在樓梯上抹眼淚、太大的頭巾滑下來遮眼，球球替牠掀起頭巾，兩隻都聽見下方轉角的喊聲。舊圖沒有樓梯與轉角。
event_lost_kitten.scene: SETTING: a short flight of four worn brown stone steps (the same brown stone as the step in reference image 3) going DOWN toward the left, where the bottom of the stairs turns around the corner of a low grey stone wall. A tiny BLACK KITTEN (the lost kitten of reference image 3: a small round black kitten with pink inner ears) sits on one of the steps, wiping its tears with one front paw, tear drops on its cheeks. On its head is a navy ninja headband that is FAR too big for it (no bell, no bow). Qiuqiu stands on the step beside the kitten, bending down gently, and with his right paw lifts the front of the kitten's oversized headband up off its eyes, so the kitten's big teary eyes peek out from under it. Both of them turn their heads toward the bottom of the stairs on the left, ears perked up, because a voice is calling from around the corner down there: a few short curved sound lines come out from behind the wall corner (no words). No other cats are visible - the caller is hidden around the corner. QIUQIU'S COLOURS: his fur is the warm pale pinkish-cream of reference image 1 with grey-brown stripes - NOT cool grey; his face is the same pale cream as his head, with only the small white muzzle of reference image 1.
refs: a later picture of this same event: copy the little BLACK KITTENS' look (small round black kittens with pink inner ears) and the worn brown stone step. The lost kitten is the one wearing the too-big navy headband - in THIS picture its headband has NO bell and NO red bow yet. Take only the kitten's look and the stone, not the composition.

event_lost_kitten_r0.why: 球球冷灰色；照結果文字重對：送回同伴身邊，小黑貓把兩個忍具塞進球球手裡、揮爪道謝。同伴照 r2 畫成小黑貓（舊圖是一隻三花貓），場景對齊新主圖的樓梯轉角。
event_lost_kitten_r0.scene: SETTING: the bottom of the same worn brown stone stairs, at the corner of the low grey stone wall, as in reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event). The lost kitten still wears its too-big navy headband, now pushed up off its eyes (no bell, no bow). The lost kitten raises one open paw and waves it at Qiuqiu to say thank you, beaming. Qiuqiu bends down a little and smiles kindly at it, like a gentle big brother.
